parsed.reason: Strong on grounding: it names the chair method plainly as the one recommendation, mentions Ferber in a clause, uses the playbook's 3-night chair steps, the 6:30-8 bedtime, the 20-30 minute routine, the extinction burst on night 2 or 3, the 2-3 week timeline, the never-lock-the-door rule and the snoring doctor trigger, and it names a check-in day. It makes no medicine, phone number or guarantee claims. Weaknesses: (1) "walk her back to her own room and sit in that night's chair spot" is an improvised night-waking protocol; the playbook only says to treat wakings like bedtime for Ferber, so this is minor and arguably consistent. (2) The "3 Bs" order of routine skips the feed-before-book detail, which is minor. (3) It says "no harm" for the five-year follow-up, whereas the playbook says "no differences, positive or negative", a slight overstatement. (4) The "why worth doing" line is thin and the plan never states the actual benefit of the skill. (5) The nights 4-6 mapping, "chair mid-room" then door then hallway, is compressed and omits the beside-the-crib stage and the "then gone" endpoint, so the parent can't tell when they have finished. (6) It is not clear that the chair goes in her room because she is moving out of the parents' bed; the plan assumes she has a crib or bed and never covers the case where she is bed-sharing. The "working" signal is fairly good. Overall it is a solid, grounded plan with minor gaps.
